newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica to buy 25 pct stake in Antena 3.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica to buy 25 pct stake in Antena 3.

text.p: Spanish telecommunications firm Telefonica de Espana said on Thursday it agreed to buy a 25 percent stake Antena 3 and would take control of the television channel.
Spanish banks BCH and Banco Santander have agreed to buy a further 18.7 percent stake, Telefonica said. The two banks already holds stakes of around 10 percent each, Telefonica added.
"Telefonica will acquire 25 percent of the shares of Antena 3 Television, while Santander and BCH will increase their current holdings, acquiring 18.7 percent," Telefonica said in a statement.
Telecommunications sources said Telefonica would pay around 21 billion pesetas for its 25 percent stake and the two banks would pay around 17 billion pesetas for their stake.

"The valuation of Antena 3 Television, made by different investment banks, reaches 95 billion pesetas," it said. As part of the deal, Telefonica will take control of 49 percent of GMA, which in turn owns 40 percent of Audiovisual Sport.
Audiovisual Sport is a unit of Antena 3, which together with Televio de Catalunya and Sogecable, controls the rights to Spain's lucrative football broadcasting.
Santander and BCH will each hold a one percent stake in Audiovisual Sport, Telefonica said. Telefonica could not give a breakdown of how much Santander and BCH would each acquire in Antena 3.

Telefonica said it had not yet agreed the exact amount that it would pay for its 25 percent stake, which would be determined at a later date and would take into account the development of other multimedia projects.
Santander said it was sure its acquisition would optimise shareholder value.

"The high quality of the technological partner -- Santander holds two percent of Telefonica's capital -- and the prospects for share diversification of the channel through its eventual launch on the bourse, have been key elements in this operation," Telefonica quoted a Santander spokesperson as saying.
